task_instance: Design a PostgreSQL schema for a small SaaS support-desk app (customers, agents, tickets, ticket_comments, tags with a many-to-many junction), applying the skill's data-type, constraint, and indexing rules, from a written requirements/access-pattern spec.
evidence: Read the SKILL.md (a PostgreSQL schema-design best-practices guide). Wrote requirements.md (entities, access patterns, scale targets, invariants) as the user-supplied input a designer would normally be given. Produced the deliverable as schema.sql: full DDL for 6 tables applying the skill's rules -- BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY surrogate keys, TEXT instead of varchar(n), TIMESTAMPTZ for all event times, status as TEXT+CHECK (not ENUM) for an evolving business value, NOT NULL+DEFAULTs, manual B-tree indexes on every FK column, LOWER(email) unique expression indexes for case-insensitive uniqueness, a composite (status, created_at DESC) index plus a partial index for the hot open/pending subset, a JSONB metadata column with GIN index and jsonb_typeof CHECK, a junction table (not an array) for the tickets<->tags relation, deliberate ON DELETE actions, and an XOR CHECK enforcing a comment has exactly one author kind. Verified the deliverable in design_notes.md with a rule-by-rule checklist mapping each core skill rule to where it is satisfied in schema.sql, plus confirmation that none of the skill's forbidden types (serial, timestamp, varchar(n), money, char(n)) appear. Files produced: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/b273891e-4b73-5af7-9840-fc512af93809/scratchpad/real2_work/r110/requirements.md, /schema.sql, /design_notes.md. Limitation: the skill's optional EXPLAIN-based index validation and migration/apply steps need a running PostgreSQL server, which this no-code runtime cannot execute; those were validated by static reasoning instead. The core stated deliverable (the PostgreSQL-specific schema design) is a text artifact and was fully produced and verified.
